To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the axon reflex-related hyperaemia induced by short (10 s) local heating of the forearm is reproducible, that it is not affected by local cooling or by the presence of a local anaesthetic, that it is abolished by a local anaesthetic and that it is not related to the local temperature.

(1) the axon reflex-induced vasodilation is reproducible; (2) the axon-reflex induced vasodilation is not dependent on the duration of the local heating; (3) the axonreflex induced vasodilatation is dependent on the temperature of the local heating.
(i) the axon reflex-induced local hyperemia is reproducible in the human skin and (ii) the axon-reflex-induced local hyperemia can be inhibited by the application of a topical local anesthetic.
